caption: The drawing shows a large, lidded tankard with a smooth metallic appearance, executed in pencil or graphite on a cream-colored paper background. The tankard has a slightly flared cylindrical body with a domed, stepped lid that includes a thumb rest and hinge mechanism. The body is decorated with a patterned border of repeating leaf motifs along the base and just above the bottom rim. The handle is ornate, curving outward with decorative elements that include sculpted faces and a floral motif; an enlarged detailed view of the handle is provided in an inset at the upper right, where markings and additional decorative features are visible. At the lower right, there is a small, outlined schematic diagram showing the tankard in profile, accompanied by dimension notations. In the upper left corner, a stamped or drawn circular emblem depicts a crowned figure and contains inscriptions in Latin, likely referencing the origin or producer. The drawing is signed "G.P. Sanborn" in the lower right. The composition is orderly, with the main tankard centered and the insets providing supplementary detail. The whole drawing is contained within a rectangular border. The colors used are shades of grey for the pencil work and a beige tone for the paper.
title: Silver Tankard
